prefilters.name: name_filter
prefilters.output: name_id_bitset (bitset over name.id, size = max_name_id+1) AND parallel name_row_for_id map via name__id__pos
prefilters.notes: Scan name parallel: read gender byte first (fast filter), then memmem 'Ang' on name varlen. Insert n.id into bitset. Also remember row position so we can read MIN(n.name) later.

prefilters.name: aka_name_person_bitset
prefilters.predicate: person_id in name_id_bitset (i.e., person exists in aka_name AND survived name filter)
prefilters.notes: Scan aka_name/person_id.bin once: if person_id in name_id_bitset, set aka_person_bitset[person_id]. Used to enforce n.id = an.person_id (semi-join with aka_name).

prefilters.name: company_us_bitset
prefilters.notes: Scan company_name; for matching rows set bitset[id]=1. Used to test mc.company_id at probe time.

prefilters.name: title_year_filter
prefilters.output: list of title rows (id, row_pos) surviving — drives outer loop

join_order.probe: movie_companies via primary CSR on movie_id
join_order.notes: For each surviving title.id v, iterate mc rows in [mc_off[v], mc_off[v+1]). Apply mc.note NOT NULL AND (LIKE '%(USA)%' OR LIKE '%(worldwide)%') AND mc.company_id in company_us_bitset. Skip title if no mc survives.

join_order.probe: movie_info via primary CSR on movie_id
join_order.notes: For each surviving title.id v, iterate mi rows in [mi_off[v], mi_off[v+1]). Apply mi.info_type_id == release_dates_info_type_id AND mi.info NOT NULL AND (LIKE 'Japan:%200%' OR LIKE 'USA:%200%'). Skip title if no mi survives.

join_order.probe: cast_info via primary CSR on movie_id
join_order.notes: For each surviving title.id v, iterate ci rows in [ci_off[v], ci_off[v+1]). Apply ci.role_id == actress_role_id AND ci.note IN voice_set AND ci.person_role_id >= 0 AND ci.person_id in name_id_bitset AND ci.person_id in aka_person_bitset. Read ci.note via offsets; compare against fixed 4-string set.
Use char_name__id__pos: row = pos[person_role_id]; require row >= 0. (person_role_id may be NULL/-1 — exclude.)

filters.predicate: note NOT NULL AND (LIKE '%(USA)%' OR LIKE '%(worldwide)%') AND company_id in us_set
info_type_id=release_dates AND info NOT NULL AND (LIKE 'Japan:%200%' OR LIKE 'USA:%200%')
role_id=actress AND note IN voice_set AND person_id in filtered_name_set AND person_role_id valid

data_structures.name_id_set: bitset over name.id space (max ~6M) — fast set membership test on ci.person_id
data_structures.aka_person_bitset: bitset over name.id space — semi-join with aka_name
data_structures.voice_note_set: small inline match: 4 string_view literals compared by length-then-memcmp
data_structures.name_row_lookup: use name__id__pos to recover name row from ci.person_id for reading n.name in aggregate
data_structures.aggregation: two running mins (string_view) — single-row scalar aggregate, no hash table needed

parallelism.notes: Partition the surviving title list across 12 threads. Each thread maintains thread-local MIN(n.name), MIN(t.title); merge at end. Prefilters (name scan, aka_name scan, company_name scan, title year scan) also run parallel over their row ranges.

indexes.purpose: fetch name row for MIN(n.name) projection from ci.person_id
(optional) confirm title row position; titles already scanned linearly

notes: Drive on title (smallest dimension after year filter). Outer-most filters reduce title to ~200k. For each title we probe three fact tables via their primary CSR (movie_id-sorted). The most selective predicates (mi LIKE pattern, ci.note IN voice_set, name filter) are pushed down into the inner CSR-range scans. The name+aka_name semi-join is pre-materialized as two bitsets over name.id space so the ci.person_id check is two O(1) bit tests. Anti/semi-join with char_name is a single pk_pos lookup. No hash join is required anywhere — every join is either a CSR range scan or a dense PK position lookup.
